content.thinking:
I'm checking the root रुच् — it's anudāttet, so ātmanepada, and it's a seṭ root, which matters for forming the āśīrliṅ uttama puruṣa ekavacana form.

Since it's seṭ with the iṭ augment, it's not jhal-ādi, so liṅsic doesn't become kit here, meaning guṇa applies to give रोचिषीय, parallel to एधिषीय for similarly-formed seṭ roots.

I'm tracing the root in the Dhatupatha — it looks like लुन्टँ in the curadi class with meaning "to steal," and I'm checking whether the न् before ट् is just phonetic assimilation (parasavarna) of an underlying लुण्ट्, or whether the nasal is actually part of the root itself.

Applying णिच् to curadi gives लुण्टि, then forming ashirlin parasmaipada (uttama dvivachana) through णेरनिटि lopa of णि before यास्व, I arrive at लुण्ट्यास्व as the final form, with न्→ण् assimilation before ट्.
I'm noting that the root ओखृँ is parasmaipada, belongs to the bhvādi class with ṛ̃ as an indicatory marker, and forms its future (lṛṭ) as ओखिष्यामि since it's seṭ.

I'm working through the root लुञ्ज् and its causative aorist formation with caṅ, checking whether the upadhā needs lengthening and tracing the reduplication pattern for the abhyāsa लु, along with the sanvadbhāva rule application.

Since the syllable after abhyāsa is guru (conjunct ñj), the sanvallaghuni rule doesn't apply, so no dīrgha happens, giving the form अलुलुञ्जम्. I'm also confirming parasmaipada applies since ṇic roots are ubhayapada by rule, finalizing अलुलुञ्जम् as the answer.
मील् is parasmaipada, bhvādi class - checking the lan uttama purusha eka vachana form, which gives अमीलम्.
I'm checking प्लुष् (plush), a bhvādi parasmaipada root meaning "to burn," with its present forms प्लोषति and प्लोषसि.

I'm looking at the root दाप् meaning "to cut," noting it's anudātta and aniṭ, excluded from the ghu-classification despite its dā-form. The p is just an it-marker, leaving dā as the true root, and I'm working through whether its aorist follows the gātisthā pattern with luk elision.

Since this root is explicitly excluded from ghu-samjñā, the sic-luk rule doesn't apply here. Instead, being an ā-ending root, it takes sak-augment with iṭ in the aorist, giving forms like अदासिषम्, अदासिष्व, अदासिष्म — so the first person dual is अदासिष्व.

I'm identifying the root म्रुन्चुँ as belonging to the gatau (motion) category, bhvadi class, parasmaipada — working out that the nasalized न् form points to म्रुञ्चु rather than the plain म्रुचु variant, giving present म्रुञ्चति and imperfect अम्रुञ्चः.
For the root śam (class 4, parasmaipada), forming the ashirlin uttama ekavachana gives śamyāsam, using the yāsam ending.
I'm working out the root रूष् (bhvadi, parasmaipada, seṭ) and forming its iṭ-aorist in parasmaipada, checking whether vṛddhi applies to the halanta vowel per the "ataḥ halādeḥ laghoḥ" rule.

I'm checking the root ओविजी in tudadi class — it's marked ātmanepadī (vijate, udvijate, "to fear/tremble"), distinct from the similar root वि in rudhadi class which I need to verify separately.

For the aorist, the sūtra 1.2.2 "विज इट्" makes the iṭ-augment ṅit after vij, which blocks guṇa, giving the lun form अविजिष्ट (with upasarga: उदविजिष्ट). The niṣṭhā participle, by ओदितश्च, would be विग्न.

I'm tracing the root भू in the curadi class, meaning mixing or thinking (अवकल्कने), and checking whether it belongs to the ātmanepadī subgroup that begins with आकुस्म in the Dhatupatha's special rule listing.

Right, "भू अवकल्कने" is the curadi dhātu meaning mixing/thinking, taking ṇic and becoming ubhayapadī by default rule for causatives. I'm working toward the benedictive parasmaipada dual form, which should come out as भावयात्.
घ्रा becomes जिघ्र by rule 7.3.78, since it's Parasmaipada - so in लट् uttama ekavacana it's जिघ्रामि.

The root क्षपि is इदित्, so नुम् gets inserted giving क्षंप्, and as a curadi root it takes णिच् to form क्षम्पयति, with लृट् giving क्षम्पयिष्यति in parasmaipada. I'm trying to recall whether this root is optionally causative per the dhatupatha listing, but I'll settle on क्षम्पयिष्यति as the answer.
Śuṣ is divādi, anudātta, aniṭ, so by the puṣādi-dyutādi-ḷditaḥ rule it takes the aṅ aorist forms: aśuṣat, aśuṣatām, aśuṣan, with the dual third person being अशुषताम्.

I'm working through the root "mā" in Āśīrliṅ ātmanepada for madhyama bahuvacana, tracing the -sīdhvam suffix and applying the sūtra on ghumāsthā roots before hal-initial affixes (6.4.66).

Since mā isn't a ghu root, the kit designation from sthāghvor icca doesn't apply to it the way it does for sthā, so I'm concluding the correct form is māsīṣṭa (without guṇa substitution), distinguishing it from how ghu roots like dā or sthā would form their counterparts.
The root भण् is parasmaipadi, so for the benedictive (आशीर्लिङ्) in parasmaipada, first person dual, the form should be भण्यास्व.

I'm identifying the root अग् from the Dhatupatha, meaning crooked motion, as bhvādi parasmaipada seṭ, and working out the luṅ (aorist) form with the sic-affix and āṭ augment, giving आग् as the stem before adding endings.

Since अग् begins with a vowel rather than a consonant, the vṛddhi rules under ataḥ halādeḥ laghoḥ don't apply, so I keep the form without vṛddhi and derive the full set of aorist forms through iṭ-sic, sic-lopa, and the standard endings, arriving at आगीत्, आगिष्टाम्, आगिषुः, and for second person singular, आगीः.
The anudātta marking on the ऋ in शीकृँ indicates this root is ātmanepadī, so for kartari voice it should take ātmanepada endings rather than parasmaipada.

I'm checking the root शुन्ध् in curadi meaning purification, forming अशुन्धयन् as the lan 3rd plural parasmaipada since curadi roots take णिच् and become ubhayapada. I want to verify whether this root is actually listed in curadi or if it's bhvadi's शुन्ध शुद्धौ instead, since there might be confusion between similar entries in the Dhatupatha.
I'm checking whether तुण (कौटिल्ये) is idit in tudādi — it isn't, since idit would require तुणिँ, so no num augment applies; with śa and no guna, the uttama bahuvacana in vidhiliṅ comes out as तुणेम.

I'm trying to recall whether curadi also lists a चि root distinct from the svadi चिञ् (चयने), searching my memory for entries like "चित सञ्चेतने" or "चिति स्मृत्याम्" and wondering how the causative form would be derived for this curadi sense.

Working through the causative formation with णिच्, applying vṛddhi (चि → चै → चाय) and considering sutra 6.1.54 which allows an optional ā-substitution for चि before णि, giving alternate forms चाययति and चापयति — and extending this to future tense forms like चाययिष्यामि.

I'm checking the root भृजीँ (भर्जने, "to roast") — the anudātta accent on ī marks it Atmanepada, so āśīrliṅ uttama dvivacana gives भृक्षीवहि. I need to confirm whether this root is seṭ or aniṭ before finalizing the form.
The root फुल् is parasmaipada, so for the benedictive (Ashirlin) third person singular, since the yasuT affix is kit and blocks guna, the form comes out as फुल्यात्.
I'm recalling the pibati conjugation pattern, checking that the third person plural form is pibanti.

I'm checking the root ष्टुच् (प्रसादे) in the Bhvadi section — the anudātta marking on the अनुबन्ध indicates it's ātmanepadī, giving the form स्तोचते.

Taking guṇa, the root becomes स्तोच्, so the विधिलिङ् ātmanepada uttamapuruṣa bahuvacana form is स्तोचेमहि.

I'm checking the accent marking on this root to determine if it belongs to the ātmanepada group, recalling that roots like द्राघृ, श्लाघृ, and लाघृ in the Bhvādi class are grouped together as ātmanepadī roots with the "सामर्थ्ये" sense.

Since this is seṭ and ātmanepada, I form the āśīrliṅ uttama puruṣa bahuvacana as ध्राघिषीमहि.

I'm tracing the root दसि from the curādi gaṇa with its णिच् derivation to दंसयति, checking whether it belongs to the ātmanepadī ākusmīya group alongside roots like चित and दंशि.

Given it's listed as ātmanepadī, the laṅ form should be अदंसयत.

रिह् is tudadi class, parasmaipada, taking श with no guna, giving the stem रिह. Building out the optative paradigm, I get रिहेत्, रिहेताम्, रिहेयुः for third person, and the first person singular form comes out to रिहेयम् — so for the middle-person singular I need, the answer is रिहे.
For jham, checking if it's seṭ for luṭ — since jham isn't in the anudātta root list, it takes iṭ, giving झमितास्थ for second person plural.
The anudatta marker on this root signals it's atmanepadi, so I'm working out the madhyama purusha dual form in lat lakara: कश् combines with आथे, with no vikarana insertion, giving कशाथे.
The root roḍ belongs to bhvādi, parasmaipada, is ṛ-it so optionally takes aṅ in luṅ, and is seṭ. For lṛṭ, I get roḍiṣyati, with dual form roḍiṣyataḥ.
The root गर्व् (garva darpe) is bhvādi parasmaipada, so for laṅ uttama dvivacana, I'm deriving गर्व्+शप्+वस् which lengthens to अगर्वाव by the ato dirgho yañi rule.

The root प्रुष् is bhvādi, parasmaipada, meaning "to burn/scorch," and is seṭ since उदित् only applies to ktvā forms. Applying guna to the इष्य affix gives प्रोष्, so the lṛṭ form for madhyamapuruṣa dvivacana is प्रोषिष्यथः.

The root धृष् (प्रसहने) belongs to curadi class, falling under the आधृषाद्वा group that optionally takes णिच्, giving forms like धर्षयति or धर्षति. I'm now checking whether this root is ātmanepada or parasmaipada within the curadi class.

Without णिच्, this root defaults to parasmaipada. Computing the conditional mood first person singular with णिच्: धृष् + णिच् undergoes guṇa to become धर्षि, then adding अट् + धर्षि + स्य + अम् with इट् augment gives अधर्षयिष्यम् as the final answer.

I'm trying to recall the exact Dhatupatha entry for this curadi root meaning "to go" — checking whether it's listed as स्वर्त or ष्वर्त and where it falls in the sequence.

Working through the णिच् formation, since the upadha र् doesn't allow guna, स्वर्त becomes स्वर्ति either way, giving स्वर्तयिता as the prathama purusha, eka vachana form in लृट्.

For स्त्यै, which is anudatta/aniT, I apply sutra 7.2.73 covering यम्, रम्, नम् and आकारान्त roots, so स्त्यै becomes स्त्या by the आदेच rule. Building sic with sak and iT gives अस्त्यासिषम्, अस्त्यासिष्व, अस्त्यासिष्म, so the dual first person is अस्त्यासिष्व.

I'm checking the root yat, in the curādi class meaning "to afflict/punish" — the Siddhānta Kaumudī gives the form yātayati.

For lṛṭ second person singular, since curādi roots take ṇic and become ubhayapada, I get yātayitāsi for kartari.

I'm checking the accent marking on व्री वरणे — the anudatta on the root vowel signals it's aniT, which makes it parasmaipada. So for lun, being aniT, I need to use sic with vrddhi.

Working through the sic formation: व्री + सिच् + सि, with the अपृक्त rule adding ईट् to avoid a single-consonant ending, giving अव्रैषीत् for third singular and अव्रैषीः for second singular. So lat is व्रीणाति, and lun forms are अव्रैषीत्, अव्रैष्टाम्, अव्रैषुः for third person, with अव्रैषीः for second singular.

I'm tracing the root पडिँ गतौ with its idit marker giving nasal पण्ड्, and the anudatta accent on the vowel signals it's ātmanepada, yielding पण्डते — so the first person plural present form is पण्डामहे.

I'm trying to recall which gana the root स्फुटिर् विशरणे belongs to, weighing whether it's bhvādi or tudādi and whether it takes ātmanepada or parasmaipada endings.

I'm trying to recall whether "स्फुटिर् विशरणे" belongs to bhvādi parasmaipada, forming स्फोटति, and whether there's a separate root for the curādi "भेदने" sense versus this one—the dhātupāṭha references I'm drawing on aren't fully settling the exact classification and gaṇa placement.

Going with parasmaipada and seṭ, I settle on अस्फोटिष्याम as the first person plural lṛṅ form.

I'm checking the accent marker on घुट् — the anudatta indicates it belongs to the dyutadi group, which is ātmanepadi by default, alongside verbs like द्युत, रुच, and लुठ.

For vidhiliṅ kartari ātmanepada, applying guṇa to the root gives घोटेरन्.

I'm examining the root दुहिँर् with its इ-anubandha, which triggers नुम् insertion giving दुंह्. I'm checking whether this bhvādi root is seṭ or aniṭ, given it ends in ह् and appears related to the duh/prapū group.

So इर् is irit, not idit, meaning no num augment — giving present दोहति. These bhvadi roots are seṭ, confirmed by forms like अतुहत्/अतोहीत् in luṅ, so the luṭ form would be दोहिता with dual दोहितारौ.
For शिल् (tudādi, parasmaipada, seṭ), applying guṇa to the penultimate vowel before sya since it's ārdhadhātuka with iṭ, giving śeliṣya, so lṛṅ 2nd singular comes out to अशेलिष्यः.

I'm working out the conjugation of पीव् (bhvadi, meaning स्थौल्य) to get पीवन्ति in lat 3rd person plural, checking whether any upadha-related guna rules apply given the root's long ī vowel before a single consonant.

I'm identifying the root शिजिँ् (अव्यक्ते शब्दे, "to make an unclear sound") as adadi-ganī and anudattet, which means it takes atmanepada and gets the num-augment, giving शिञ्ज्. Working through lat uttama purusha eka, I arrive at शिञ्जे.
I'm trying to identify the root मेडृँ, checking whether it falls under bhvadi and whether it's parasmaipada or ubhayapadi, comparing it against similar roots like मिदृँ/मेदृँ in the Dhatupatha.

I'm trying to pin down the root मेथृँ॑ in the Dhatupatha—checking its accent marks and whether it's ubhayapadi, since this affects how I classify its grammatical properties.

Finding it listed as "मिथृँ॒ मेथृँ॒ मेधाहिंसनयोः," confirming it's ubhayapadi and seṭ (since it's not on the anit list). For Luṭ kartari, the parasmaipada form works out to मेथितास्थ, combining मेथिता with स्थ.
The root मत्रिँ (गुप्तपरिभाषणे) belongs to curādi gaṇa and falls in the ākusmīya list, making it ātmanepadī, so the present tense form is mantrayate, and the future (lṛṭ) form becomes मन्त्रयिष्यते.

Working through viś in the conditional: applying guṇa gives veś, then the sibilant shifts to ṣ, and the following s becomes ṣ as well, producing vekṣya. Adding the 2nd person dual conditional ending yields avekṣyatam.

I'm trying to pin down whether घूर्ण भ्रमणे belongs to bhvādi as ātmanepada or tudādi as parasmaipada, checking which conjugation class gives घूर्णति versus घूर्णते.

For the vidhiliṅ madhyama bahuvacana form, I'm working out that it should be घूर्णेत.

I'm tracing the root रुसि in the curadi class, which takes नुम् augment due to its इदित् marking, giving रुंस् as the base, with causative forms like रुंसयति and periphrastic future रुंसयिता.

Since curadi roots with णिच् allow both पदs due to कर्त्रभिप्राय, taking parasmaipada here gives second person plural रुंसयितास्थ as the final form.

I'm tracing the root छदि in the curadi class, which forms छन्दयति, and checking whether it's ubhayapadi since curadi roots typically take णिच् and both padas — working out the first-person plural future form अच्छन्दयिष्याम while also noting a separate root छद meaning concealment.
The anudatta marking confirms कत्थ् is atmanepadi, giving कत्थते. So the lan third person dual atmanepada form is अकत्थेताम्.

I'm looking at the root लघिँ with its anudatta accent marking it as atmanepadi, meaning the इ marker signals num agama giving लङ्घ्, and this is a seṭ root in the gatyarthah sense from the dhatupatha.

For the lut atmanepada third person plural, the forms match parasmaipada's तारः ending, so I get लङ्घ् + इट् + ता forming लङ्घितारः.

I'm trying to locate the root "nad" in the curādi gaṇa and checking whether the initial ṇ reduces to n, then working through how adding the causal suffix would trigger vṛddhi of the upadhā to form "nādi".

Given curādi's bhvādi-style conjugation, the lṭ (future) form comes out as nādayiṣyanti, with the pada determined by whether the fruit of the action accrues to the agent.
The root शेल् belongs to the bhvādi class, parasmaipada, with stem शेल. For the optative (vidhiliṅ) third person dual, the form comes out to शेलेताम्.

I'm working through the root पचिँ, adding the नुम् augment to get पञ्च्, then deriving the curadi present पञ्चयति and the लुङ् aorist form through चङ्, checking whether reduplication applies since the उपधा is ञ् rather than a vowel.

Since the root syllable is guru due to the conjunct, सन्वद्भाव (इत्व) doesn't apply, giving the abhyāsa प and the form अपपञ्चत for both 3rd and 2nd singular. I'm also confirming the padi designation — though this root could take ubhayapada via णिचश्च since it's a curadi root, the parasmaipada form remains अपपञ्चत for 2nd plural as well.
I'm working out the root मूल् (मूलँ), bhvādi class, parasmaipada, seṭ — forming the periphrastic future मूलिता, and for first person plural मूलितास्मः.
I'm checking whether द्राडृ is marked anudatta (indicating atmanepada), tracing it through the Dhatupatha classification, and working out the lan prathama ekavachana form as अद्राडत.
मिष् is parasmaipada, so for vidhiliṅga prathama puruṣa bahuvacana I get मिषेयुः.

The root वृजीँ (curadi 10.267, meaning "to avoid") takes the causative affix with guṇa, giving वर्जि, so the future tense form becomes वर्जयिष्यति. Since curadi causatives are ubhayapada, I need to derive the parasmaipada second-person plural form: वर्जयिष्यथ।

I'm checking the root उध्रस in the Dhatupatha, meaning उञ्छे — noting that some grammarians treat the initial उ as an इत् marker, giving forms like उध्रासयति/ध्रासयति per Siddhanta Kaumudi.

Applying णिच् to ध्रस् gives उपधा वृद्धि, yielding उध्रासि, and in लुट् the 2nd person plural form becomes उध्रासयितास्थ.

I'm examining the root णेषृ (gatau, bhvadi, ātmanepada due to the anudātta marking), checking how it forms in luṅ. The ṛ-it status seems relevant mainly for caṅ formations with ṇic, not for plain luṅ, so I'm setting that consideration aside.

The root itself is udātta and seṭ, so in luṅ with sic, the ātmanepada third person singular form comes out as अनेषिष्ट.

I'm checking the root षू (प्रेरणे) in tudādi gaṇa - it's parasmaipada, and I'm working out whether it's seṭ, since monosyllabic roots ending in ū typically take seṭ augment.

Looking at the exception rule 7.2.44 (svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūditir vā), I note that sūti (adādi) and sūyati (divādi) are vet, but tudādi सू is not covered by this exception, so it remains seṭ. This gives me sāvitā for the future and asaviṣyat for lṛṅ, so the 3rd person plural would be असविष्यन्.

I'm trying to recall whether वृतुँ belongs to the curadi gana's भाषार्थाः group, and noting that the udit marker उँ signals it's इदित्, requiring num insertion to give वृन्त् as the stem.

For the causative form, since the upadha is न् (not laghu in the usual guna sense), I get वृन्तयति without guna modification.

Working through लुङ् with चङ्, I'm checking reduplication rules — since वृ followed by the conjunct न्त् makes it guru rather than laghu, सन्वल्लघुनि doesn't apply, giving अववृन्तत् for third singular and अववृन्ताम् for third plural. I'm second-guessing whether वृतुँ truly falls under the भाषार्थाः group in curadi, trying to recall the exact list from Siddhanta Kaumudi.

Actually I realize वृतुँ carries the उँ anubandha, making it उदित् rather than इदित्, so नुम् doesn't apply here — that rules out my earlier वृन्तयति derivation. Instead वृत् with laghūpadhā guṇa gives वर्तयति as the causative, and for लुङ् with चङ्, the optional ऋत्व rule (उर्ऋत्) lets the ऋ-vowel base alternate between वृत् and वर्त्, yielding both अवीवृतत् and अववर्तत् as valid third singular forms.
The root उठ् belongs to bhvādi parasmaipada, and since it has a light penultimate उ, guṇa applies giving ओठ्, so the present tense forms become ओठति, with the dual second person as ओठथः.
